note: On profile this is close to the textbook case and fails only on money. He is a self-employed professional photographer taking six-week international commissions, married, considering children, career explicitly advancing — the 'or equivalent' end of the occupation test. Health is the classic neglected corner: a lifelong cycle of getting fit for an event and then declining, described by him as 'a sick cycle'. He is emphatically good-to-great rather than rescue, saying 'I've never had a problem with the way I look when I'm working out' and wanting to record his peak lifetime strength, and at 6'0" and around 195 lb with solid kettlebell fundamentals, a multi-minute deep squat and an athletic history he is the opposite of the deconditioned exclusion. The income criterion fails on willingness rather than obvious incapacity: he anchored unprompted at $100-150 a month, balked at $200, and cited competing financial commitments. That combination is the finding — a profile-perfect prospect whose price expectation sits an order of magnitude below the offer, and who was routed to a $200-a-month product rather than being sold or disqualified on the flagship.
